I wrote 46 acceptance tests for W2-48 and committed them as `ceb4ec1d`. All 46 fail for the expected reasons: the cache does not exist yet. Along the way I settled the interface the engineer must build to, and I raise four questions for you below (P-1 to P-4).

task: Write W2-48's (DAEO-xxgp) FULL acceptance tests from its KPI lines and sources, before any implementation, and show them red.
status: PACKAGES — the tests are committed and red for the stated reasons; P-4 must be answered before the engineer can make the close-level cases green, and P-1 to P-3 are confirmations of forms I settled.

Role, ticket, top-level folder and branch matched (`independent-test-designer`, `DAEO-xxgp`, `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-48`, `w2/W2-48`). I wrote 46 cases in 12 test files, plus a support module, a conftest and a README. Every record is checked against a log the planted tests write when they really run, so a test marked "passed" must actually have run. I checked every fixture against today's `gov close` in a throwaway script outside the tree, and calibrated what plain pytest-testmon selects on the planted suite. Nothing is left outside my test folder.

The hooks folder held only `*.sample` files before the commit. `gov.__file__` is `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-48/src/gov/__init__.py`.
tests: Ran `PATH=…node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH PYTHONPATH=…/W2-48/src python3 -m pytest tests/acceptance/W2-48 -q -p no:cacheprovider -rs` to its end, twice. Result both times: 46 failed, 0 skipped, 0 passed (33.8 s before the commit, 100.4 s after it). The collection check over all tests ended with `14731/14733 tests collected (2 deselected) in 26.79s`, with no collection error. My folder adds exactly 46; the 2 deselected tests also appear without my folder and with testmon disabled, so they come from the base.
discoveries: (1) pytest-testmon 2.2.0 and coverage 7.16.2 were installed at 14:17:03 today, during this session, so the install package Q-13 has landed. My first check at the start said testmon was missing. (2) testmon 2.2.0 crashes when pytest's cache provider is off: `--testmon -p no:cacheprovider` gives `INTERNALERROR KeyError: 'lf'`, and `gov close` passes that option on every run. The cache's folder could instead be moved out of the tree with `-o cache_dir=…`. (3) When testmon's data version (SQLite `user_version`, 14) does not match, testmon deletes its file and starts fresh without saying so; the cache must notice this to report it. (4) Plain testmon with `-n 2` re-runs exactly the test that uses a changed module or fixture, but does not see a change reached only through a subprocess at all; that gap is this ticket's real work. (5) In this repository `gov close` runs under the pinned release's interpreter (`~/.local/share/gov-os/pin-fecb870c/bin/python`, a venv), while leads run `/usr/bin/python3`; testmon keys on installed packages, and the pin's own `gov-os` package could stop leads from ever reusing the close's results. (6) This repository's `.gitignore` covers neither `.testmondata` nor `.coverage*`, and `.gitignore` is outside the ticket's paths; cache files must live under `.gov-runtime/` or the next close refuses its own tree. (7) The KPIs pull two ways: "the test command and its options" is an input, yet leads must reuse the close's results. I settled it: the command key leaves out which tests are selected, and a lead's run runs suites exactly as the close does. (8) When testmon deselects every test, pytest exits 5 ("no tests ran"); together with the close's rule that an acceptance run in which no test passed is refused (DEC-487), a re-close after a refusal could be refused wrongly. The flaky-test case covers this.
risks: The forms below are my settlement; a different choice (a `gov testcache` command, other folders) means a designer revision. One case, `test_subprocess_coverage_lets_an_unchanged_test_that_starts_a_process_be_reused`, rests on my reading of DEC-852 (P-3). The research-record check is keyword-based. Once green, the suite will be slower: about 25 closes and many cached runs, each `gov close` bounded at 180 s and each cached run at 600 s. If a cached run is made with xdist workers but without the cache provider, it fails at startup because of discovery (2).
lessons: `gov retrieve` gave nothing here: this worktree has no store (`STORE_MISSING`), and against the main tree's store both the lexical and semantic facets were stale (`FACET_UNAVAILABLE`), so I read the named files directly. Running plain pytest-testmon on the planted suite in a scratch folder is a quick way to check that a "must be reused" demand is within the tool's reach before writing it. Read refusals from the guard: 0. Sandbox refusals: 1, when `uv python list` could not write its cache lock in `~/.cache/uv`; I did not retry it. The expected refusal of sandbox check (a) is not counted.
proposed_decisions: P-1, commands as `python3 -m gov.testcache run|command|nightly` rather than a new `gov testcache` command; recommend (a) as written, confidence high. Choosing (b) would need an owner decision like DEC-542 plus revisions of W1-07's recorded command list and W1-32's `test_the_command_set_is_the_twelve_and_the_three_recorded_ones`; under (a) no earlier test needs revising. P-2, the interpreter class: this machine has only Python 3.12.3, so the planted change is a venv of the same version with one extra installed package; recommend (a) accept this now, and (b) a second Python version as an install package only if the owner wants the version itself proven, confidence medium-high. P-3, DEC-852's "or": recommend keeping subprocess coverage as the mechanism, with "always re-run" only where coverage cannot follow a process; dropping the one case above is the alternative, confidence medium-high. P-4, `gov close --no-cache` and the call from close need `src/gov/close/command.py`, but W2-48 may only touch `src/gov/close/cache*` and W2-07 holds the rest; recommend widening W2-48's paths by that one file, for the option and the call only, confidence high. Full six-part packages are in the README.
unresolved: Answers to P-1 to P-4. The figures in the research record are the engineer's to produce. The two deselected tests come from the base.
recommended_next_action: Answer P-4 (widen W2-48's paths by `src/gov/close/command.py` for the option and the call), confirm P-1 to P-3, then start the engineer, telling them about the testmon cache-provider crash (2), the silent version drop (3) and the interpreter mismatch (5) as context.

**Forms I settled (the interface the implementation must provide):**
- **Commands.**
  - `gov close <ticket> [--no-cache] --json`.
  - A lead's run: `python3 -m gov.testcache run [--no-cache] --json [<path>…] [-- <extra pytest options>]`. Paths default to `tests`. It runs suites exactly as `gov close` does, including the project's `close_workers` (`-n`). Extra options after `--` count as another command.
  - A non-pytest command: `python3 -m gov.testcache command [--no-cache] --json [--input <glob>]… -- <program> [<argument>…]`. Without `--input` it always runs.
  - The nightly: `python3 -m gov.testcache nightly [--ref <branch>] [--record <path>] --json`. `--ref` defaults to `w2/integrate`. It runs in its own checkout outside the main tree, never under `.gov-runtime/` (DEC-673).
  - The full uncached run for W2-24 and W2-46 is `run --no-cache`.
- **Exit codes and envelope.** API-0002 envelope. Exit 0: every test passed or was reused from a pass, record in `result.test_cache`. Exit 3: something failed (code `TESTS_FAILED`), or the nightly named a cache fault, record in `error.details.test_cache`. Exit 1: governance error.
- **The record `test_cache`.**
  - Fields: `run`, `commit`, `clean`, `cache` (`used` / `off` / `unreadable`), `reason`, `engine` (names `pytest-testmon <version>` and `coverage <version>`), and `tests`.
  - Each entry of `tests` is `{id, result, from?}`. The id is the pytest node id relative to the project root; a file that failed to collect gets its own entry with the file path as id and result `error`.
  - `from: {run, commit}` names the run that last actually ran the test.
  - `gov close` carries the same block in its close record's frontmatter.
  - The nightly adds `ref` and `cache_faults: [{id, result, cached, from}]`.
- **Declared inputs.** The path map's `test_inputs` lists globs for configuration, data and the dependency lock. pytest's own ini file and the interpreter with its installed packages count as inputs of every test without being declared.
- **Unseen inputs.** `@pytest.mark.unseen_inputs("<kind>")`, kind one of `dynamic-import`, `outside-read`, `network`, `clock`. Any use means the test runs every time.
- **Where entries live.**
  - Shared entries: `<main tree>/.gov-runtime/testcache/shared/`, written only by a close from a clean tree.
  - A run's own entries: `<its tree>/.gov-runtime/testcache/local/`, never read by a close.
  - A worktree finds its main tree through git.
